clue.text: Come back for fruit after harvest.

indicators.note: after places the fruit behind the harvesting word in the answer

parts.note: to reap is to harvest a crop
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Fruit reappears on the trees once the harvest is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is the charade signal: the fruit comes second, behind the harvesting verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappear is to return into view, to come back.

clue.text: Fundamental sort of nerve required to imprison a Communist leader

indicators.note: to imprison means one piece is locked inside the other

parts.note: the radial nerve runs down the arm

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of Communist

explanation.surface: Nerve is needed to jail a top communist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required' is a link; 'leader' gives C from Communist, placed inside RADIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Radical means going to the root, basic or fundamental.

clue.text: It helps pilot with tailspin to take a measurement

parts.note: read as tail spun round, giving its letters jumbled
to meter is to measure

explanation.surface: A pilot in a tailspin needs an instrument reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailspin' looks like an aviation crisis but means TAIL in a spin: ALTI.
explanation.definitionFit: An altimeter is a cockpit instrument showing height, so a pilot's aid.

clue.text: End contract holding up work

indicators.note: holding means the first word keeps the other inside it

parts.note: to purse your lips is to contract them

indicators.note: up in a down clue reads the word for work from bottom to top

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Ending a contract delays the job.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the work word from bottom to top, and 'holding' puts it inside the lip-tightening verb.
explanation.definitionFit: End and purpose both mean an aim or goal.

clue.text: Maintenance for some luxury vehicle included

indicators.note: included means the vehicle sits within the other word

parts.note: any means some, as in have you any
a limo is a luxury car

explanation.surface: Maintenance costs are covered for a luxury car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; LIMO goes into ANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Alimony is money paid for an ex-spouse's support after divorce.

clue.text: The art of the law.

explanation.surface: A grand phrase about legal skill, the art of the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Mosaic is an art of setting tiles; the Mosaic law is the code given through Moses.

clue.text: Intervention with drugs knocking .. out cold

indicators.note: knocking out means a letter is struck from the drug word

parts.note: medication means drugs
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A medical intervention with drugs leaves a patient out cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking out cold' reads as anaesthetic, but C (cold) is knocked out of MEDICATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediation is stepping in between parties to settle a dispute.

clue.text: Slender thing holding a revolver

parts.note: not a gun holder, but a thin rod on which something turns

explanation.definitionFit: A spindle is a thin rod or axle around which a wheel or bobbin rotates.

clue.text: Select group, a sort of maniple

indicators.note: sort of suggests a variant arrangement of the letters of maniple

explanation.surface: An elite band is like a Roman maniple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a link. A maniple was a Roman army unit, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: To impanel is to pick a jury, choosing a group of people.

clue.text: Check backcloth. for set

parts.note: to check someone is to deter them

indicators.note: back tells us the word for the cloth is read from end to start

parts.note: denim is a cotton cloth

explanation.surface: A theatre hand checks the backdrop for the stage set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backcloth' looks like stage scenery, but it splits into 'back', the reversal signal, and 'cloth', the fabric of jeans.
explanation.definitionFit: Set and determined both mean resolved, firmly fixed on a course.

clue.text: Warrior's sanctimonious admission?

parts.note: an admission or confession starting I'm, short for I am
pi is slang for pious or sanctimonious

explanation.surface: A warrior smugly admits his own piety.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical reading: a sanctimonious person might admit 'I'm pi'. PI is old school slang for pious.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a Zulu regiment or band of fighting men.

clue.text: Unremarkable choice of recreational area

parts.note: a common is open public land for recreation
or is the word that offers a choice
a garden is also a place for recreation

explanation.surface: Picking between two parks is an unremarkable choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'choice of recreational area' reads as either one park or the other: COMMON, OR, GARDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Common-or-garden is an idiom for ordinary, nothing special.

clue.text: Extremely lucky to catch animal — pure chance

indicators.note: to catch means the outer letters hold the animal between them
extremely asks for the extremes, the first and last letters of lucky

parts.note: an otter is an animal

explanation.surface: Being lucky enough to catch some creature is pure luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives the first and last letters of lucky, L and Y, and 'to catch' puts OTTER between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery is any outcome decided purely by luck.

clue.text: Well thought of, but pure disaster on the board

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second
disaster suggests the letters of pure are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: a table and a board are both flat surfaces where meals are served

explanation.surface: A respected company suffers a pure disaster at board level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link; in a down clue 'on' stacks the jumbled word above the board.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputable means having a good standing, respected.

clue.text: Join sack race a little lighter

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
to fly is to race along quickly

explanation.surface: Entrants are invited to join a sack race as a little light relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Join' simply tells you to put the two pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: A firefly is a small insect that gives off light, so a tiny lamp of sorts.

clue.text: Where the dogs may sit for warmth?

definitions.text: Where the dogs may sit for warmth?

parts.words: Where the dogs may sit for warmth
parts.note: suggests pets by a hearth, but firedogs are iron supports for logs in the hearth

explanation.definitionFit: Firedogs, or andirons, stand in the hearth of a household fire.

clue.text: . Could be exercise with sharp jerks

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: jerks suggests the letters of sharp are jolted into a new order

explanation.surface: Perhaps this is an exercise class full of sharp, jerky movements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerks' looks like gym movements but is the anagram signal; school sport supplies the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Perhaps and could be both express possibility.

clue.text: Fence — without its ends, it's going to fail

indicators.note: without signals that letters are taken away from the fence
ends says the letters removed are the first and last

parts.note: its points back to the fence just named
to lose is to fail

explanation.surface: A broken fence without its posts is going to collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its ends' refers to the fence: drop its first and last letters to get ENC, then add LOSE; 'it's going to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To enclose is to surround with a barrier, as a fence does.

clue.text: Beagle misses nothing, going over colourful part of county

indicators.note: going over in a down clue puts the first piece above the second
misses means a letter is lost from the dog word

parts.note: a beagle is a kind of hound
O stands for nothing, zero
red is a colour, so colourful

explanation.surface: A beagle wanders over a bright corner of the shire.
explanation.walkthrough: A hundred was an old subdivision of an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically English shires were divided into districts called hundreds.

clue.text: Infirm, say? Would shortly be protected

parts.note: split as in plus firm, and firm is sure, giving in sure
would shortened is the contraction 'd

explanation.surface: A frail person asks whether they would be covered by a policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Infirm' looks like a medical word but splits into IN + FIRM, and 'say' invites a synonym for firm, SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being insured means being covered by a policy against loss.

clue.text: Sacred chant in American city two notes short

indicators.note: short means the city lacks something

parts.note: Detroit is a city in Michigan
D and E are musical notes

explanation.surface: Hymns are sung in an American city, a couple of notes short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops DE, two notes of the scale, from DETROIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An introit is a psalm or anthem sung at the start of Mass.

clue.text: Ray, as a star, getting a broad smile

parts.note: the sun is a star
a beam is a wide smile

explanation.surface: A man called Ray, a celebrity, flashes a big grin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a name but is the definition; 'as' and 'getting' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbeam is a single shaft of light from the sun.

clue.text: Engines fail and less gets shunted

parts.note: to die is to fail, as an engine dies

indicators.note: gets shunted suggests the letters of less are moved around like rail wagons

explanation.surface: Locomotives break down and fewer get moved in the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets shunted' is the anagram signal, borrowed from railway yards to suit the engines.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesels are compression-ignition engines, or locomotives powered by them.

clue.text: Old city name not special? Not special

indicators.note: special in the sense of specially made, so the preceding letters are fashioned anew

explanation.surface: A puzzled query whether an old city name is special, answered no.
explanation.walkthrough: The last 'special' is the anagram signal: N + NOT + SPECIAL + NOT are rearranged into the fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Constantinople was the former name of the city now called Istanbul.

clue.text: It's the end for each of us in time

indicators.note: the end for picks the final letter of each

parts.note: of us means belonging to us, our

explanation.surface: A grim reminder that death comes for every one of us in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; the surface's deathly 'end' is really the last letter of each.
explanation.definitionFit: An hour is a unit of time.

clue.text: Sir Walter Elliott's favourite reading, except one quotation at end of volume

parts.note: bar means except, as in all bar one
a tag is a short quotation

indicators.note: at end of selects the closing letter of volume

explanation.surface: A literary character loves one book, apart from a single quotation at its close.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Walter Elliot in Jane Austen's Persuasion never read anything but the Baronetage, a register of baronets.
explanation.definitionFit: In Persuasion, Sir Walter's chosen book is the register of titled families of his rank.

clue.text: Tamper with sound of gong

indicators.note: sound of means the word is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal or decoration

explanation.surface: Someone tampers with a gong to change its ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gong' is not the percussion instrument but British slang for a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle is to interfere or tinker with something.

clue.text: Hold back majority of lesson, having no support

parts.note: to stem is to hold back a flow

indicators.note: majority of means most of the word lesson, losing its tail

explanation.surface: A teacher cuts short most of a lesson, leaving it unsupported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'majority of' drops ON from lesson to give LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stemless describes a flower or plant without a stalk to hold it up.
